Summary.Name: DeepCORO-JEPA
Summary.Description: One EchoJEPA video encoder (ViT-L) that segments the coronary tree into 26 SYNTAX classes itself and, from up to 12 diagnostic coronary angiography runs per study, predicts for each coronary segment the % diameter stenosis, the probability of a significant lesion, the probabilities of calcification, thrombus and chronic total occlusion (CTO) and, from model v19, the probability that the segment is 100% occluded (shown as "100% (occluded)" on the 12 epicardial segments above a validation threshold) and the probability that a stent is visible (annotation only); plus LAD FFR and iFR (proximal and mid LAD, value and probability of an abnormal result), study-level lesion probabilities and the coronary dominance. 17 segments are supported: the posterior left ventricular branch (lvp) has no training target, so its values are returned for compatibility but are not meaningful, never raise a flag and are never displayed. When the caller sends the view label of each run, the segments of a coronary side with no run are returned as not assessed. The encoder runs at most twice per study: full views at 224 px, then up to 4 tracked 320 px crops per segment. Version 2.2.0 serves model v19 (point release v19.2), released by the principal investigator's decision although its pre-registered release rule was not met. Earlier working name: DeepCORO-Integrated.
Summary.Training_run: Weights & Biases run 78768630 of project mhi_ai/deepcoro-segmentation: https://wandb.ai/mhi_ai/deepcoro-segmentation/runs/78768630 (test inference run mrs2l28c)

Mechanism.Outcome: Per-segment coronary stenosis, 100% occlusion, calcification, thrombus and chronic total occlusion (17 supported segments), possible stent, study-level lesion probabilities, LAD FFR/iFR (proximal and mid LAD) and coronary dominance
Mechanism.Output: model_version (v19); segments.<segment>.stenosis_pct (0-100, the model estimate), .display_pct (integer 0-100, the % shown in the report) and .display_category (normal, mild, moderate, intermediate, severe, occluded), .prob_significant (label: >= 70%, left main >= 50%), .prob_threshold, .significant (true when prob_significant > prob_threshold), .calcif_prob, .calcif, .thrombus_prob, .thrombus, .cto_prob, .cto (each flag true when its probability > the threshold of that finding); unsupported_segments (["lvp"]): segments.lvp keeps its numeric keys, has unsupported = true, its four flags are always false and it has no display_pct or display_category; lesion_thresholds.operating_point, .calcif, .thrombus, .cto; study_lesions.study_calcif_prob, .study_thrombus_prob, .study_cto_prob (probability that the finding is present in any segment; no yes/no call); lad_physiology.ffr, .ifr, .ffr_abnormal_prob (FFR <= 0.80), .ifr_abnormal_prob (iFR <= 0.89), .ffr_abnormal_threshold, .ifr_abnormal_threshold, .ffr_abnormal, .ifr_abnormal, .operating_point; model_dominance.dominance_left_prob (probability of a left-dominant circulation), .dominance_left_threshold, .dominance_left_pred (true when the probability > the threshold), .operating_point, .label_source; coronary_dominance (only when the caller sent additionalMetadata.coronaryDominance; it alone decides how the schema is drawn); n_videos, encoder_passes From 2.2.0 (model v19): segments.<segment>.occluded_prob, .occluded (true on the epicardial segments of occluded_threshold.segments when occluded_prob > occluded_threshold.threshold, 0.50), .occlusion_tag (CTO when the CTO flag is set, else acute/other; empty when not occluded); .stent_prob and .possible_stent (stent_prob > stent_annotation.threshold, 0.0891; annotation only); .assessed = false and .not_assessed_reason on the segments of a coronary side with no run among those read (side check; flags false, no display fields); occluded_threshold.threshold, .operating_point, .segments; stent_annotation.threshold; side_check.available, .left_runs, .right_runs, .not_assessed_side, .not_assessed_segments, .dominance_side (or .reason when not available); lad_physiology.region ([prox_lad, mid_lad]), .region_label, .region_segments, and .assessed = false without a left coronary run. A v19 segment with occluded = true has display_pct 100 and display_category occluded; a CTO flag alone no longer shows 100%.
Mechanism.Target_population: Adults undergoing diagnostic coronary angiography at MHI
Mechanism.Input_data_source: Diagnostic left and right coronary contrast runs (multi-frame XA DICOM)
Mechanism.Model_type: Deep learning: EchoJEPA ViT-L video encoder with its own segmentation decoder, tracked segment crops and per-segment attention pooling; stenosis and lesion (calcification, thrombus, CTO) heads on each segment; a study-level lesion reader over the full-view tokens; LAD physiology head on the left main / LAD / diagonal features; a coronary dominance head on the pooled segment features

Model.Purpose: Read stenosis severity and three lesion findings in every coronary segment and estimate LAD physiology from the angiogram alone
Model.Output: 18 stenosis percentages, probabilities and yes/no calls (17 supported; the posterior LV branch is unsupported); 18 x 3 lesion probabilities and yes/no flags; 3 study-level lesion probabilities; LAD FFR/iFR values, abnormal probabilities and yes/no calls; probability of a left-dominant circulation and its yes/no call; from v19: 18 occlusion probabilities (shown 100% on the 12 epicardial segments above 0.50) and 18 stent probabilities (possible-stent annotation)

Uses_and_directions.General_use: Research preview of segment-level stenosis and lesion reading, image-only LAD physiology estimation and coronary dominance estimation.
Uses_and_directions.Target_population_and_use_case: Adults with diagnostic coronary angiography. Upload the diagnostic left and right coronary contrast runs (no PCI, stent or ventriculography runs); up to 12 are used, chosen by SeriesTime. Send runs of both coronary sides: a side without a run cannot be read (with view labels, its segments are returned as not assessed).
Uses_and_directions.Before_using_this_model: Held-out test (3,194 studies / 2,941 patients, read once; 95% patient-bootstrap confidence intervals). Release status: model v19 did NOT meet its pre-registered release rule and was released by the principal investigator's decision (2026-11-20) on a post-hoc endpoint, occlusion detection (epicardial segments, AUPRC 0.461 [0.413, 0.513] against 0.384 for the CTO probability of model v16, +0.077 [0.038, 0.116]). Stenosis macro AUROC 0.879 over 17 segments (v15 0.877, DeepCORO-CLIP 0.850); mean per-segment Pearson r 0.519 (0.507-0.532); mean ICC 0.440. LAD FFR/iFR pooled AUROC 0.705 (0.634-0.771; 270 proximal or mid LAD measurements; v15 0.674). Lesion findings, AUPRC mean over segments / pooled: calcification 0.121 / 0.179, thrombus 0.404 / 0.327, CTO 0.136 / 0.172. "100% (occluded)" at the display threshold 0.50 (epicardial, 462 occluded / 31,442 non-occluded segments): sensitivity 0.34 [0.30, 0.38], specificity 0.997, PPV 0.63 [0.57, 0.69]; of the segments shown occluded, 63% were reported 100%, 14% 90-95%, 4% 70-89% and 20% below 70%. Dominance AUROC 0.946 against labels derived from another model. Confirm every reading on the images.

Warnings_and_limitations.Input_selection: The model was trained only on diagnostic left/right coronary contrast runs without stents. This version does not filter uploads; PCI, stent, ventriculography or non-contrast runs degrade the output (segments with a visible stent are annotated 'possible stent').
Warnings_and_limitations.Distal_and_branch_segments: Agreement with the cath report is weaker for the posterolateral branch, distal LAD, distal LCx, diagonals, marginals and ramus (r 0.24-0.45 on test).
Warnings_and_limitations.Physiology: LAD FFR/iFR outputs reach AUROC 0.71 on test (0.705, 95% CI 0.634-0.771, 270 proximal or mid LAD measurements; FFR alone 0.75 on 76, iFR alone 0.69 on 194) and do not replace invasive measurement. The pressure labels are proximal or mid LAD measurements only: the predicted call refers to that region (returned as lad_physiology.region and marked in the report when abnormal), not to a culprit lesion located by the model. Without a left coronary run (side check) the pressure output is not assessed.
Warnings_and_limitations.Video_encoding: DICOMs are converted exactly as the training videos (MJPG AVI). About 13% of training/test videos had been stored as MP4; for those studies the DICOM path differs slightly from the AVI-based test results.
Warnings_and_limitations.Displayed_stenosis: The stenosis estimate is pulled toward the mean. The report shows a rescaled value (display calibration cal1 refitted on v19, data/stenosis_display.json): an estimate below 10.5% is shown as 0% (normal); above, the knots 10.5->20, 23.5->30, 33.5->50, 42.5->70 and 100->100, rounded down, so the category boundaries are exactly at 23.5, 33.5 and 42.5. Fitted on the v19 validation split (78,999 segment readings of 17 segments). Agreement with the report category on validation: 19% and weighted kappa 0.37 for the raw estimate; 66% and 0.59 for the mapping (66% and 0.59 in 5-fold patient cross-validation); 62% and 0.58 with the rule that a flagged segment is never shown as normal. A segment with occluded = true is shown "100% (occluded)" instead (takes precedence over the mapping and the flag rule); the v19 % head is trained only on segments below 99%, so the estimate of an occluded segment is conditional (median about 55%) and is never shown in place of the occluded display. Two thirds of occlusions are not shown as 100% and show their %. The v15 and v13 mappings are kept only to redraw stored results of those models.
Warnings_and_limitations.Confidence_Scores: Probabilities are not calibrated. The yes/no calls use thresholds chosen on the internal validation set, not validated clinical operating points; a call is positive when probability > threshold. Stenosis, pressure and dominance use the threshold with the highest geometric mean of sensitivity and specificity. On the held-out test set: FFR <= 0.80 at 0.4805: sensitivity 0.72, specificity 0.70 (76 measurements); iFR <= 0.89 at 0.5999: sensitivity 0.61, specificity 0.69 (194); significant stenosis, mean of the 17 supported segments: sensitivity 0.78, specificity 0.80, PPV 0.25, NPV 0.98. Left dominance at 0.0204 on the validation set.
Warnings_and_limitations.Flags: Thresholds of rarely diseased segments are low (for example 0.0082 for distal LCx), so a segment can be flagged with a low probability and a low estimated percentage. At least one segment is flagged for stenosis in 41% of test studies without any significant lesion in the report and in 97% of those with one (dossier figures, computed with the posterior LV branch flag, which this container never raises). FFR and iFR are separate outputs and their calls can disagree in the same study.
Warnings_and_limitations.Lesion_flags: Calcification, thrombus and CTO are rare, so their flags use one threshold per finding set for 99% specificity on the validation set (calcification 0.3809, CTO 0.1343; the v15 CTO override 0.70 is dropped in 2.2.0 because a CTO flag no longer shows 100%). On the held-out test set: calcification sensitivity 0.19, specificity 0.989, PPV 0.26; CTO sensitivity 0.36, specificity 0.990, PPV 0.19. The thrombus flag uses the fixed threshold 0.40 (kept since 1.4.1): validation sensitivity 0.21, PPV 0.25; test sensitivity 0.38, PPV 0.42. Most findings are missed and most flags are false: an absent flag does not exclude the finding. Lesion labels come from the angiography report.
Warnings_and_limitations.Study_level_lesions: study_lesions gives one probability per finding for the whole study (any segment). It has no threshold and no yes/no call, and the release dossier reports no performance figure for it: treat it as an uncalibrated score.
Warnings_and_limitations.Dominance: model_dominance is the model's own estimate of a left-dominant circulation. Its training and evaluation labels were derived from another model (majority over the right coronary videos), not read by experts, and it is less reliable in studies without a right coronary run. It is reported as text and does not change the schema: the schema follows the caller-supplied coronary_dominance (angiogram classifier majority) when present and is drawn right dominant otherwise.
Warnings_and_limitations.Unsupported_outputs: The posterior left ventricular branch (lvp) had no training target in model v19 (as v15). Its keys stay in the JSON for compatibility; the numbers are not meaningful, its flags are always false, it has no display fields and it is never shown in the report, the diagnosis or the explanations. The post-PCI outputs of model v15 (stent, final TIMI flow, failed PCI) need post-PCI runs as input and are not produced by this container.
Warnings_and_limitations.Occlusion_display: "100% (occluded)" uses P(occluded) > 0.50 on the 12 epicardial segments (left main, proximal/mid/distal LAD, LCx and RCA, PDA, posterolateral), chosen by the principal investigator on the validation set (sensitivity 0.35, specificity 0.997, PPV 0.66) from a menu; the pre-registered 95%-specificity point 0.22737 (validation PPV 0.18) is not used. Branches (diagonals, marginals, ramus) are never shown occluded. The CTO / acute/other tag follows the CTO flag (0.1343) and has no separately validated threshold: on test 91% of reported CTOs, 76% of other occlusions and 73% of false displays were tagged CTO, so the tag is weak.
Warnings_and_limitations.Possible_stent: possible_stent is an annotation, not a flag: the procedure head's P(stent visible) above 0.0891 (95% specificity among untreated segments on the v19 validation post-PCI rows, 25,222 segments, 2,469 treated: sensitivity 0.44, PPV 0.49, AUROC 0.85). On pre-PCI diagnostic studies it marks 2.4% of segments (29% of studies), many of them old stents or restenosis, so the grade is always kept. The model was trained on diagnostic runs without stents; post-PCI runs are read less reliably.
Warnings_and_limitations.Side_check: The model always outputs all 18 segments. In single-side studies (26% of validation studies) the unseen side reads poorly (r 0.27 for the RCA in left-only studies and 0.22 for the left segments in right-only studies, against 0.64 / 0.50 when imaged). When additionalMetadata.coronaryViews gives the view label of every run read, the segments of a side with no run (RCA, or left main / LAD / diagonals / LCx / marginals / ramus; PDA and posterolateral follow the dominance) are returned with assessed = false and are not reported. Without view labels the side check is not available and every segment is reported.
Warnings_and_limitations.Comparison_with_v15: Model v19 replaces v15 (v16 was never deployed). Against v16, its parent, on the same test studies: stenosis is unchanged (mean r -0.000 [-0.004, 0.004]; macro AUROC -0.001), the pressure output is not distinguishable (-0.018 [-0.038, 0.002]) and occlusion detection is better (AUPRC +0.077). Against v15: macro AUROC 0.879 against 0.877, mean r 0.519 against 0.507, pressure AUROC 0.705 against 0.674.

Changelogs.2.2.1: 2026-11-23: Same model (v19.2), weights, thresholds and probabilities as 2.2.0. Report fixes only: the CTO performance line states the threshold it was measured at, and region flags agree with their segments when the left side is not assessed (PR #519).
Changelogs.2.2.0: 2026-11-21: serves model v19 (point release v19.2; Hugging Face heartwise/DeepCORO_JEPA@6e192eb, branch v19, tag v19.2; weights 8af2e27a...7eed; W&B run 78768630), released by the principal investigator's decision although the pre-registered release rule was not met (post-hoc endpoint: occlusion AUPRC). New per segment: occluded_prob / occluded / occlusion_tag ("100% (occluded) - CTO / acute/other" above 0.50 on the 12 epicardial segments), stent_prob / possible_stent (annotation only, threshold 0.0891 re-derived on v19 validation post-PCI rows), and assessed / not_assessed_reason from the side check (additionalMetadata.coronaryViews). lad_physiology names its measurement region (proximal and mid LAD), shown in the report when FFR or iFR is abnormal. The CTO flag uses v19's specificity_99 threshold 0.1343 (the v15 override 0.70 is dropped) and no longer shows 100% by itself. Display calibration cal1 refitted on v19 (10.5 / 23.5 / 33.5 / 42.5). Results stored by 2.0.0 and 2.1.0 (v15) and by 1.x (v13) render as their containers drew them.
Changelogs.2.1.0: 2026-11-15: Same model (v15), weights and probabilities as 2.0.0. The CTO flag now needs a probability above 0.70 instead of 0.2134 (Thresholds.lesion_threshold_overrides; returned operating point: specificity_99 (thrombus: fixed 0.40, cto: fixed 0.70)), the model owner's choice for a higher positive predictive value. On the v15 validation split (78,999 segment readings of the 17 shown segments, 551 with a chronic total occlusion in the report): at 0.70, 172 segments are flagged, 57 with a CTO in the report (PPV 0.33, sensitivity 0.10) and 107 with a CTO or a 100% stenosis in the report (0.62); at 0.2134, 1,017 are flagged (PPV 0.18; 0.40 counting any reported occlusion; sensitivity 0.34). The PPV does not rise above about 0.33 at any threshold. Not evaluated on the test set. A CTO flag draws the segment as occluded and shows 100%, so fewer segments are shown occluded; cto_prob is unchanged and results stored by 2.0.0 keep their flags.
Changelogs.2.0.0: 2026-11-15: Numbered 2.0.0 because new weights are a major version under the release policy. The PyTorch build of this image is not the one the test metrics were computed with: it is numerically close to the evaluated model, not identical. On 300 validation studies accuracy is equal (17-segment mean correlation 0.4933 against 0.4932); an individual stenosis estimate differs by 0.25 points in median, 2.9 at the 95th percentile and rarely much more (49 at most), and some yes/no calls differ. The test-set metrics were not recomputed with this build. The image installs PyTorch 2.11.0 built for CUDA 12.8 instead of 2.14.1 built for CUDA 13.0, which could not use the GPUs of a server with an NVIDIA 570 driver. Serves model v15 (Weights & Biases run 2563ce01, Hugging Face revision ab6d12f, tag v15.1) with its own thresholds. New in the JSON, no existing key changed: model_version, study_lesions (study_calcif_prob, study_thrombus_prob, study_cto_prob; probability only), model_dominance (dominance_left_prob, dominance_left_threshold 0.0383, dominance_left_pred), unsupported_segments. The posterior LV branch (lvp) has no training target in v15: its keys stay, its flags are always false, it has unsupported = true and no display fields. Display calibration cal1 refitted on the v15 validation split (below 9.5 -> normal; 9.5->20, 21.5->30, 34.5->50, 49.5->70, 100->100; rounded down); the report header reads v15-cal1. /inference/render-report draws a stored result with the display values, calibration note, performance figures and header of its own model version: a v13 result (1.1.0 to 1.4.1) is never given the v15 mapping. The thrombus flag keeps the fixed threshold 0.40 (v15 validation: 166 segments flagged, 43 with thrombus, PPV 0.26, sensitivity 0.215; not evaluated on the test set). The caller-supplied coronaryDominance is unchanged and still decides the schema; the model's own dominance is shown as text. Test set against v13: stenosis slightly lower (mean r 0.508 against 0.521), pressure not distinguishable (0.674 against 0.689), lesion detection better (thrombus AUPRC 0.402 against 0.304).
Changelogs.1.4.1: 2026-11-15: Same model (v13) and weights. The thrombus flag now needs a probability above 0.40 instead of 0.0851 (Thresholds.lesion_threshold_overrides in models/config.json; returned operating point: specificity_99 (thrombus: fixed 0.40)). Chosen on the validation split of the served weights (4,647 studies, 200 segments with thrombus in the report) to raise the positive predictive value: at 0.40, 60 segments are flagged, 18 of them with thrombus in the report (PPV 0.30, sensitivity 0.09), against 902 flagged, PPV 0.08 and sensitivity 0.36 at 0.0851. No threshold reaches a PPV of 0.80 on more than one segment. Not evaluated on the test set. thrombus_prob is unchanged; results stored by earlier versions keep the flags they were computed with. Calcification and CTO thresholds are unchanged.
Changelogs.1.4.0: 2026-11-14: Same model (v13), weights and thresholds; stenosis_pct and every flag unchanged. Display calibration cal1 of the stenosis estimate: each segment gets display_pct and display_category, and the report (schema labels, segment detail, summary and diagnosis text) shows display_pct, with 0% worded as normal (estimate below 10%). A segment flagged for significant stenosis is never shown as normal. The report header reads v13-cal1 (reportModelVersion). The mapping (below 10% -> 0%; 10->20, 23->30, 37->50, 51->70, 100->100) was fitted on the validation split of the served v13 weights, without the posterior LV branch rows (weak report grading); it is applied to every displayed segment. Schema drawing of the lesion flags (drawing only): a calcified segment lies on a grey band with calcium plates, the vessel distal to a CTO flag is drawn grey (no antegrade flow shown), and a thrombus flag is drawn as a clot symbol in the lumen.
Changelogs.1.3.0: 2026-11-13: Same model (v13), weights, thresholds and report. POST /inference/render-report draws the HTML report of a stored JSON-mode result (identical to HTML-mode predict for the same prediction) on the CPU without loading the model; model-info advertises capabilities.renderReport. predictions.explainability[i].images (crop and frame, base64 JPEG) is now kept in the JSON so a stored result renders with its pictures.
Changelogs.1.2.0: 2026-11-13: Same model (v13), weights and thresholds. The HTML report draws the 18 segments on a coronary schema instead of a table. An optional additionalMetadata.coronaryDominance (study majority of the angiogram procedure classifier over the diagnostic videos sent) is validated, returned as predictions.coronary_dominance, added to the diagnosis and used to draw the schema left or right dominant. In the report and diagnosis a CTO-flagged segment is shown as occluded at 100% (stenosis estimate kept in the JSON), thrombus flags are drawn as a filling defect, and the posterior LV branch is not shown (still in the JSON). For each flagged stenosis segment (up to 6) the report shows the tracked crop with the highest attention, the within-crop attention the model applied (recomputed exactly from the same forward call) and the full frame with the crop box; the JSON gets the matching metadata in predictions.explainability without images.
Changelogs.1.1.2: 2026-11-12: Same model (v13), same thresholds and same code. The image now installs PyTorch 2.14.1 built for CUDA 13.0 instead of 2.5.1 built for CUDA 12.1, so it also runs on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. Returned numbers differ slightly from those of the development environment in which the test metrics were computed (44 of 8,880 yes/no calls on 120 test studies; same AUROC to 2 decimals); see the README.
Changelogs.1.1.1: 2026-11-12: Same model (v13). Probabilities are returned with 6 decimals instead of 4 and every yes/no call is taken on the returned probability, so a response never shows a probability at its threshold next to a positive call.
Changelogs.1.1.0: 2026-11-12: Serves model v13 (Weights & Biases run 400d0a77): adds calcification, thrombus and CTO probabilities and flags per segment and the Thresholds key lesion_operating_point. Stenosis is unchanged on test (macro AUROC 0.885 against 0.884); pressure AUROC is 0.69 against 0.72 for v12.
Changelogs.1.0.0: 2026-11-12: Serves model v12: 18-segment stenosis and LAD FFR/iFR with validation-derived thresholds.
